title: Flutter web Shader compilation error
body: I built my Flutter web app with `flutter build web --web-renderer canvaskit` and published it to Firebase Hosting. The published website does not work, although it works in debugging mode. Chrome DevTools reports a shader compilation error. I can reproduce it with my public repository and hosted website. I am using Flutter stable 3.16.4 on macOS 14.1.

symptoms_visible: My CanvasKit website does not render after publishing it to Firebase Hosting, but the same app works in debugging mode.
Chrome DevTools shows a shader compilation error when I open the published site.
N0.label: N0 published CanvasKit site fails

symptoms_visible: The published site fails in Chrome Beta on my Intel Mac, while it works in the other browsers I tested.
The problem occurs only with CanvasKit rendering.
N1.label: N1 browser and renderer isolated

symptoms_visible: The published site remains blank in the failing Chrome browser even though WebGL and WebGL2 are listed as hardware accelerated.
Out-of-process canvas rasterization is disabled in both the failing Chrome Beta and a working stable Chrome.
N2.label: N2 GPU configuration collected

symptoms_visible: After removing the extra code and keeping only the list of circular avatars, the published site still produces the same error.
The console prints CONTEXT_LOST_WEBGL followed by a shader compilation error whose source samples a texture and applies a circle mask.
N3.label: N3 reduced reproduction and shader log

symptoms_visible: On an affected Intel Mac, the same exception remains after enabling Out-of-process 2D canvas rasterization and relaunching Chrome.
I cannot require customers to change a Chrome experimental flag before they can render the page.
N3_x.label: N3_x browser-flag workaround rejected

symptoms_visible: A network JPG or JPEG makes the release app fail, while the same test works with PNG, WebP, or GIF.
A profile or release build made with browser image decoding disabled renders the JPG case successfully.
Flutter's parallax example also crashes for me when it loads its JPG image.
N4.label: N4 image path isolated

symptoms_visible: After installing and testing Chrome 123 Beta, the published JPG example still produces the same error on my Intel Mac.
N5.label: N5 newer beta still affected

symptoms_visible: After Chrome received the browser-side change, the published CanvasKit site works again on my Intel Mac, including the network JPG content.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved after Chrome rollout

question_patterns: Does the hosted site fail in other browsers, and which exact browser build and Mac architecture are affected?
Can you reproduce this in stable, beta, or canary Chrome, and is the Mac Intel or Apple Silicon?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried all browsers. It works except in Chrome Beta on my Intel x86_64 MacBook Pro. The failing build is Chrome Beta 121.0.6167.16.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It fails in every browser on both Intel and Apple Silicon, including Safari and Firefox.
It fails on a different Chrome Beta patch version, but still only on Intel macOS.

question_patterns: Does this happen only when the app uses the CanvasKit renderer?
Can you compare the CanvasKit and HTML web renderers?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, it is CanvasKit rendering only.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The HTML renderer fails in exactly the same way.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c2, c5, c9 and c12: the original reporter isolated the failure to Chrome Beta on an Intel Mac and confirmed it was CanvasKit-only. Stable and Canary initially worked and are represented as target-node volunteered information.

question_patterns: Please paste the about:gpu output from the browser that fails.
Can you provide the failing browser's GPU feature status and driver workarounds?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In the failing Chrome Beta, Canvas, compositing, rasterization, WebGL, WebGL2, and WebGPU are hardware accelerated. Canvas out-of-process rasterization is disabled. The output lists Intel Mac workarounds including `dont_use_loops_to_initialize_variables`, `msaa_is_slow`, and `max_msaa_sample_count_4`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: about:gpu says WebGL and WebGL2 are disabled and all rendering is software-only.
The same hardware-accelerated status is reported with a slightly newer Chrome Beta patch.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c14-c16: participant2 requested about:gpu and the actual failing-browser data. The reporter later compared the canvas-rasterization status with working stable Chrome and noted that both had it disabled.

question_patterns: Can you reduce the hosted example and report the smallest remaining UI that still reproduces?
Please remove unrelated code from the reproduction and republish it.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I removed the extra code and kept only `UserStories()`, which is a list of circular avatars. I published that reduced version and it still gives the same error.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The reduced app works; the failure only returns when an unrelated plugin is added.

question_patterns: Can you paste the console warnings, error, and generated shader as text rather than a screenshot?
Please copy the complete shader compilation output from DevTools.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The warnings include `CONTEXT_LOST_WEBGL` and `INVALID_OPERATION: delete: object does not belong to this context`. Then CanvasKit prints `Shader compilation error` and a 21-line shader. It samples `uTextureSampler_0_S0`, calculates distance from `ucircle_S1_c0`, clamps the circle value, and multiplies the texture color by that circle output.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There is no WebGL context loss or shader compilation output; the console only contains an HTTP 404 for an application asset.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c19 and c21-c23: the original reporter permanently reduced and republished the reproduction, then pasted the raw console warnings and shader source after participant3 requested text. The browser/Skia ownership of that shader is engineer interpretation, not part of the reporter's answer.

solution.intent: Treat enabling Chrome's Out-of-process 2D canvas rasterization flag and relaunching the browser as the resolution.
solution.concrete_example: Open chrome://flags, set Out-of-process 2D canvas rasterization to Enabled, and relaunch Chrome.

edges.comment: Messages c25-c30: participant4 proposed the browser flag as a solved resolution. The original reporter rejected requiring customers to alter flags, and participant5, another affected Intel-Mac user folded into the simulated user side, reported that the workaround did not work. Other users later found it locally effective, but the thread did not accept it as a deployable production resolution.

question_patterns: Can you reduce the image case by testing the same network image flow with JPG, PNG, WebP, and GIF files?
Does the failure depend on the network image format rather than the image widget or caching package?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested a minimal `Image.network` example. A JPG URL produces the error, while PNG, WebP, and GIF URLs work. Other affected users confirmed that changing their network JPG images to PNG or WebP makes the app render.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every image format fails, including local PNG assets, and removing all images does not change the crash.
JPEG fails while PNG and WebP work, but GIF was not tested.

question_patterns: Can you compile a profile or release build with `--dart-define=BROWSER_IMAGE_DECODING_ENABLED=false` and report whether the same JPG case renders?
Please test the provided browser-image-decoding toggle against the minimal reproduction.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: This works for me. With `--dart-define=BROWSER_IMAGE_DECODING_ENABLED=false`, the release case renders instead of failing.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The build still loses its WebGL context with browser image decoding disabled.

edges.comment: Messages c42-c52 and c63-c68: participant12 and other affected users, folded into the user side, isolated network JPG/JPEG input with a minimal format comparison. Participant14 tested participant3's build-time decoding probe and reported only the raw successful result. The original reporter separately reproduced with Flutter's JPG-based parallax example.

question_patterns: Could you test the current Chrome 123 Beta on the same Intel Mac and report whether the hosted reproduction works?
Please retry the published example in the newer Chrome Beta.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested Chrome 123 Beta and the error still exists for me on the same Intel Mac.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The hosted reproduction works reliably in Chrome 123 Beta with the default flags.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c69-c70: participant22 requested a test of Chrome 123 Beta. The reporter installed and tested it, but still observed the failure. This is raw version-test output and does not identify which Chromium change is responsible.

solution.intent: Treat this as a Chromium ANGLE-on-Metal regression affecting Intel macOS, not a Flutter shader defect; update Chrome after Chromium disables or reverts the affected experiment, then verify the hosted CanvasKit JPG case with default browser settings.
solution.concrete_example: Update Chrome after the Chromium rollout that disables the affected ANGLE Metal path on Intel Macs, restore experimental flags to their defaults, and retest the published CanvasKit site. If an immediate application-side mitigation is required before that browser update reaches users, disabling browser image decoding can avoid the failing path, with the warning that decoding then occurs on the UI thread and may cause jank.
solution.inference_hint: Engineers reproduced the GPU-process crash with ANGLE's Metal backend and determined that the failing shader was compiled by Skia inside Chromium for HTML rasterization rather than coming from Flutter's CanvasKit copy. Chromium later disabled the ANGLE-Metal experiment on Intel Macs. Those causal conclusions are engineer-side inference from the platform matrix, GPU output, shader log, and Chromium investigation; the reporter supplied only the observed test results.

edges.comment: Messages c17-c18, c60 and c72-c79: participant2/participant3 traced the problem to the Chromium ANGLE/Metal path and reported that Chromium disabled the experiment on Intel Macs. After the rollout, the original reporter and multiple affected users independently confirmed that the hosted site worked again. The final reporter confirmation is terminal-side verification, not required evidence for proposing the browser-side resolution.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause as a Chromium ANGLE-on-Metal regression on Intel macOS that crashes while compiling a browser Skia shader; it is not ultimately a Flutter-authored CanvasKit shader defect.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected platform matrix, about:gpu data, WebGL context-loss and shader output, and the network-JPG/browser-decoding probes.
Must recommend a Chrome build containing the Chromium-side disablement, revert, or fix and ask the user to retest the published CanvasKit JPG case with normal browser settings.
Must not present manually enabling Out-of-process 2D canvas rasterization as the production resolution: the reporter rejected requiring customer flags, and it failed for an affected Intel-Mac user.

Disabling browser image decoding or converting JPG images may be offered only as a temporary application-side workaround, with the UI-thread image-decoding performance cost acknowledged where relevant.
Must treat the issue as resolved only after an affected user confirms that the hosted site works after the Chrome-side rollout.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Flutter developer who can publish Firebase builds, switch Flutter channels, compare browser versions, inspect about:gpu, reduce a reproduction, paste generated shader logs, and test build-time defines.
persona_hint.communication_style: Responsive, practical, and persistent; supplies concrete environment details and public reproductions, tests requested configurations, and challenges workarounds that cannot reasonably be imposed on customers.
